Welcome to Medina House School
Welcome to Medina House School, a truly inclusive specialist primary school based in Newport on the beautiful Isle of Wight. We are a well-resourced, split site, with our main campus on School Lane, Newport with a second, but smaller site, in School Lane, Newport. We have have also opened our third site which is the Island’s first SEMH primary provision which is based in the village of Chillerton.
As a school we provide the opportunity for all pupils to thrive and succeed. Whilst focusing on pupils special educational needs, learning opportunities are adapted and scaffolded to ensure that all pupils experience success in their learning and make holistic progress over time.
Through our whole school, values-based charter, The Medina House Way (click below), all stakeholders contribute towards Medina House being a wonderful place to work, attend and visit.
If you do have any further questions or would like to arrange a visit ot the school then please do not hesitate in getting in touch.

Personal Development
Personal Development
Personal development is a core focus area of the school ethos as we see this as being directly linked to improving the life chances of our learners. As such we regard PSHE as a core subject within our curriculum. This enhanced focus recognises the importance of this subject in supporting our pupils’ life skills. Staff continuously model these skills throughout the school day to ensure that they are not only featured in cross curricular learning strands but that pupils see these being used in a variety of contexts.
Medina House has an extensive Mental Health Support Team which ensures that all pupils’ needs are being met and to ensure that they have access to these essential therapies. The team consists of two ELSAs and one play therapist who are supported by the whole school mental health lead. Mental Health Action Group meetings are held regularly to ensure that the mental health of all of our school community is considered. Any specific support required is triaged and supported through the most relevant support network, for example sign posting to relevant agencies or support from our family liaison officer.
Pupils regularly focus on the curriculum of our fundamental British Values and these are often seen ‘live’ in school. Examples of these include children being allocated classroom tasks and responsibilities, students voting for their student council representative, enrichment afternoons and celebrations. The school is active in the local community and regularly visits the local church where we celebrate yearly events such as Harvest Festival and Christingle. Although our students live on an island we are keen to ensure that they are made aware of the wider opportunities made available to them on the mainland as well as participating in events with mainstream pupils for example, sporting tournaments and Dance Live.
Medina House School prides itself on our inclusivity and ensuring that all pupils are given the opportunities to attend activities in line with their age and stage. Our focus is always to celebrate everyone as a unique learner whilst encouraging teamwork to ensure that children accept their peers. All children are encouraged to celebrate each other’s achievements in weekly class assemblies and end of term celebrations; these examples link to our successes of becoming a Rights Respecting School (Silver Award).

Admissions
As a local authority school the Isle of Wight SEN team has ultimate say on all of our school admissions. Parents should contact the local authority to find out the specific arrangements about our admission requests, including waiting lists.
– Department: SEN Assessment & Review Team – Address: SEN Assessment & Review Team, Sandy Lane, Newport, Isle of Wight, PO3O 5NA – Phone: 01983 823470 – Email: sen@iow.gov.uk
Medina House School is a community special school, with spaces for 138 boys and girls school aged 4 to 11. All the pupils who attend are directed to the school by the Isle of Wight Special Educational Needs Team and have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) which summarises assessments for education, medical and psychological.
Criteria for Admission
Pupils will have complex learning difficulties often in association with other needs or conditions and with varying needs of complexity such as:
– Speech and language disorder, impairment or delay – Physical disabilities – Autistic Spectrum Conditions – Hearing impairment – Visual impairment – Behavioural challenges
Visits to the school are warmly welcomed and these are conducted on the first Tuesday of every month. Please contact the school office if you would like to book a tour of the school.

Reading
Reading
At Medina House School, reading is a key part of our learning approach. All our staff have taken part in specialist training to better understand how to teach reading to pupils with complex learning needs. We’ve also invested in resources and tools to make sure every child can access reading in a way that works for them.
We use a nationally recognised phonics and reading programme called Little Wandle, which helps us provide a consistent and supportive approach across the school. Our school library plays an important role too; it’s a safe, welcoming and inspiring space where pupils can enjoy reading with their class, in small groups, or one-to-one.
We know that communication is closely linked with learning to read. That’s why we build in regular opportunities for pupils to practise reading in ways that suit their needs, including using communication systems like PECS and other supportive devices.

The Medina House Way
The Medina House Way
The Medina House Way serves as a whole school charter for all stakeholders. All stakeholders had a voice in its creation to ensure that it captured our key values and examples of how these can be demonstrated at school.
Staff highlight and celebrate examples of pupils demonstrating these values and these are shared in real time with parents via the Arbor portal. At the end of each term, pupils with the highest number of ‘stars’ in each category are celebrated in our Christmas, Easter or Summer church services.

Catering and Free School Meals
Catering and Free School Meals
Lunch is cooked and served at Medina House. Parents receive a copy of the menu termly. Children can choose from a range of healthy options, usually a main meal, plain pasta or jacket potato.
If your child has significant dietary requirements you must let us know and we will then endeavour to cater for them, based on their individual needs.
If you want to, you may provide your child with a packed lunch which they can eat in the hall with those having a school lunch. We ask you to provide a healthy lunch with no crisps, chocolate or fizzy drinks.
Dinner money is collected weekly on a Monday. You can pay weekly, monthly or termly. Please pay by cash. The current daily price is £3.00 per dinner
If you receive income support, your child is entitled to free school meals.
Application forms are available from the school office.
The children are provided with a healthy morning snack. We encourage children to drink water at any time during the day. All the children have their own water bottle which is available all day.
Most classes have a weekly cooking session which is related to topic work or specific areas of the curriculum.
